To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and tested an approach to determine the unfolding energy landscape of polyproteins that is more accurate than previous methods, and that we have validated this approach by determining that the energy landscape parameters are not significantly skewed by the unequal unfolding probability distribution observed in force extension experiments.

(1) there is a significant unequal unfolding probability distribution that affects the calculation of the energy landscape parameters from constant velocity force spectroscopy experiments; (2) Monte Carlo simulations incorporating the effects of the unequal unfolding probability distribution show that the calculated energy landscape parameters from the Zhurkov Bell model are not greatly impacted by the unequal unfolding probability; and (3) the minimum acceptance criteria used in force-extension experiments is justified and does not skew the calculation the energy landscape parameters.

the Zhurkov model can be used to calculate unfolding parameters for polyprotein systems, that the unequal unfolding distribution has little effect on the unfolding parameters, and that the accuracy of the unfolding parameters is limited by the number of unfolding events observed in a force-extension experiment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of the Bell model to the analysis of force-extension experiments on proteins.
the development of a Monte Carlo simulation to optimize the calculation of the parameters describing the unfolding energy landscape of proteins.
the development of an accurate method for calculating energy landscape parameters from force extension measurements of polyproteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Zhurkov Bell model is a robust method that can be used to obtain the energy landscape parameters of a protein from single-molecule unfolding experiments.

the use of Monte Carlo simulation to incorporate the unequal unfolding probability distribution into the unfolding energy landscape calculation is not required, and the minimum acceptance criteria are justified.
single-molecule force extension experiments on polyproteins are an effective method to determine the unfolding energy landscape of proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of the Monte Carlo simulation to account for the impact of the uneven unfolding probability distribution on single-molecule force spectroscopic experiments is an important tool for the calculation of energy landscapes parameters.
the Zhurkov model can be used to determine the energy landscape parameters of polyproteins, but the accuracy of the parameters is dependent on the quality of the experimental data.

the Zhurkov model is a robust method for calculating energy landscape parameters from force extension curves, and it is not necessary to correct the unfolding energy landscape parameter calculations for the observed unequal unfolding probability distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

while there is significant unequal unfolding probability distribution in single-molecule protein pulling experiments, this does not greatly affect the determination of unfolding energy landscape parameters using the Zhurkov Bell model.
the Zhurkov–Bell model is robust to a range of unequal unfolding probabilities.
the unequal probability distribution of unfolding events in single-molecule force spectroscopic experiments does not have a significant impact on the determination of energy landscape parameters.
